title: Physics-informed generative learning yields experimentally verified single-phase B2 intermetallic alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) generated candidate compositions in complex alloy systems, and an artificial neural network (ANN) scored their B2-forming probability from 18 physics-informed, composition-derived descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering. Five previously unreported CVAE-proposed compositions were synthesized and verified as single-phase B2 after homogenization: Fe2.7Co18.6Ni28.8Ti41.8Zr8.1, Fe7.4Co11.6Ni31Ti43.5Zr6.5, Fe8.8Co14.2Ni26.5Ti40.1Zr10.3, Co19.9Ni30.5Ti38.1Zr11.5 and Cu4.7Co9.2Ni36.4Ti38.7Zr7.4Hf3.5. Two alloys with low predicted B2 probability, synthesized as a negative check, did not form B2. The study reports that random-sublattice descriptors separated B2 from multiphase alloys more effectively than conventional random-mixing descriptors in these datasets.
ai_technology: Physics-informed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and artificial neural network (ANN)
organization: Central South University; City University of Hong Kong; City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan); Shanghai University

evidence.tested: After homogenization (1273 K, 24 h), XRD superlattice peaks, SEM/EDS compositional uniformity, and TEM/SAED free of antiphase-domain or phase-boundary contrast jointly established single-phase B2 (rather than BCC+B2) in five CVAE-proposed compositions. Two alloys with low predicted B2 probability were also synthesized and formed multiphase non-B2 intermetallic structures (Fig. S9). The new alloys showed Elinvar behavior over 300–750 K, and their compressive yield strength and fracture strain were measured. On the Fe-Co-Ni-Ti-Zr training data, the ANN reached 100% precision and 97.4% recall for B2, with an F-measure of 0.97 ± 0.03 across 400 independent retrainings.
evidence.unknown: The result is one paper-level experimental discovery program; individual alloys are not counted separately. Experiments validated five selected high-probability compositions from a small subset of the generated search space, not all model proposals; further compositions in the Fe-Ni-Ti-Zr and Co-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf systems are reported only in the Supplementary Information (Fig. S10) and are not counted here. Phase assignment rests on laboratory XRD, SEM/EDS and TEM; no Rietveld refinement, synchrotron diffraction or atom-probe tomography is reported. The paper makes no claim that the 18 descriptors separate L1₂, σ or Heusler phases, or that they apply to non-refractory systems. Mechanical results were mixed (the Fe-Co-Ni-Ti-Zr alloys had lower yield strength than reference CoNiTiZr); broader property superiority and generalization to arbitrary alloy systems are not inferred here. Synthesis and characterization were performed by researchers.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN learned B2-versus-non-B2 phase likelihood, P(B2), from historical alloy-composition data (a B2:non-B2 ratio of about 1:9 in the Fe-Co-Ni-Ti-Zr database) using 18 random-sublattice descriptors computed from composition rather than from measurements. The CVAE generated candidate compositions (in the Fe-Co-Ni-Ti-Zr analysis, 10,000: 5,000 B2-conditioned and 5,000 non-B2-conditioned), and compositions with P(B2) above 0.95 or 0.99 were selected for synthesis and experimental structure confirmation.

source_review.scope: Open-access version-of-record full text (Results, figure captions, Methods) reviewed for an author-requested correction from the first author (Weijiang Zhao, 2026-11-25); the corrected text uses only claims supported by the main paper. Supplementary Information not audited.
